grh_627ce2ece8a83eb2cf61.title: The Best Years of Our Lives
paragraphs: Bombardier Fred Derry, banker Al Stevenson, and Navy veteran Homer Parrish return together to Boone City after the war, each discovering that home is no longer as simple as memory made it. Homer, who lost both hands, fears that his devoted fiancÃ©e Wilma will eventually regret marrying a disabled man. Al returns to his family and banking career carrying the emotional dislocation of combat, while Fred finds that his wartime rank means little in civilian life and that his marriage to Marie cannot survive his unemployment and changed outlook. After Fred loses his drugstore job defending Homer and other veterans, he pushes Homer to trust Wilma rather than sacrifice their future out of fear. grh_627ccf0573c9142a4e09.title: Words at War 43-12-21 (28) Log Book - British Merchant Marine
paragraphs: A dramatization of Frank Laskier's Log Book follows a troubled young Englishman from reformatory life into the British Merchant Marine. Harsh ships, poverty and rough treatment nearly deepen his alienation, but fellowship at sea and wartime service give him a renewed sense of purpose. After his ship is torpedoed and he loses a leg, the sailor reflects on the social failures that shaped men like him while insisting that merchant seamen will help win the war and should also have a voice in building a better peace afterward.

The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes.

grh_626d4d26e5e885b39a8b.title: The Eager Victim
paragraphs: Claude Janik offers Shayne $1,000 to kill him and leaves a statement absolving the detective, but Janik later turns up murdered with the same gun and Shayne's fingerprints on it.
